facts.text: Ewell sits at the heart of Smith Island, the largest village on the 9.4‑square‑mile marshland community in Somerset County.
The village first appeared in 1657 when English settlers arrived, but permanent families only settled in 1686, founding a community that still thrives today.
Ewell’s only way in or out is by passenger ferry from Crisfield, Maryland, a 12‑mile ride across the Chesapeake Bay that keeps the island isolated.
The island’s low‑lying terrain—just 2 to 3 feet above sea level—makes Ewell one of the United States’ lowest‑lying communities.
Sea‑level rise and erosion have cut Smith Island’s habitable land to about 900 acres, threatening Ewell’s future despite ongoing marsh‑restoration projects.
Ewell’s economy once buzzed with 19th‑century oystering, as local watermen harvested Chesapeake oysters that fed markets across the bay.
